steps.what: Investigate service and equipment complaints through discussion and on-site inspection
Take corrective action and check that the service or equipment problem is resolved

tasks.design: Keep complaint details accessible through existing work records in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The supervisor investigates on site, agrees the remedy and checks the result; a ticket status does not establish the cause or resolution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints often need observation and discussion to distinguish service failure from equipment problems.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital records can retain evidence but do not replace investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed expectations, intermittent faults and whether corrective work actually resolves the concern.
tasks.human_edge: Listening fairly and selecting an effective remedy.
tasks.altitude: Investigation and corrective responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Safe isolation and when cleaning staff must stop use

evidence.claim: FacilityApps supports digital work orders; that does not demonstrate automated complaint investigation or corrective work.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor investigation, remedy selection and checking resolution. Cleaner rework and technician repairs are outside the focal denominator and unchanged; no transferred labour saving is claimed.
No machine depends on an assumed fault or resolution code; the supervisor produces findings in s1 and checks the remedy in s2 with full time retained.
Native work records come first. Zero upkeep because no new system or complaint procedure is introduced.
research_questions: Which complaints need on-site checks before a remedy can be chosen?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, net0 after zero upkeep. Investigation, corrective coordination and checking retain their time; no unmeasured paperwork saving is added.

steps.what: Instruct staff in policies, procedures and safe equipment use and maintenance

tasks.design: Keep approved policies and equipment instructions available in {DOCS}. The supervisor demonstrates, answers questions and observes staff practice; a searchable instruction sheet does not replace practical instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staff need to apply instructions safely in the actual workplace.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instruction access supports the session without establishing shorter coaching time.
tasks.still_hard: Language barriers, different experience and unsafe habits not revealed by a quiz.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting instruction and recognising when someone needs another demonstration.
tasks.altitude: No change to practical training responsibility or time.

evidence.claim: The digest does not establish a labour saving for live cleaning-staff instruction or equipment demonstrations.

assumptions: Boundary is live instruction and checking practice; separate policy authoring and training administration are outside it. Staff learning time remains outside the supervisor denominator and unchanged.
No machine consumes a free competence flag. The supervisor observes understanding within s1 with full time retained.
Use native access to approved documents first. Zero incremental upkeep because existing instruction practice remains unchanged.
unknowns: Required training and staff accessibility needs
research_questions: Which practical errors require demonstration rather than another written instruction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Live instruction retains full time and no material-authoring baseline is assumed.

tasks.short: Select and purchase supplies or equipment

steps.what: Establish needs for new equipment, supplies or furnishings
Select suitable items and confirm quantities, prices and delivery requirements
Check and place the order or purchase through the authorised route

tasks.design: Configure catalogue-to-order reuse in {PROCUREMENT} before building anything. Keep needs assessment and item selection human; reuse the selected lines for the order and require the authorised supervisor to confirm the exact purchase before submission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected items can be retyped into a separate order or supplier form.
tasks.enabler_now: Native purchasing configuration can reuse selected catalogue and quote fields without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Suitability, substitutions, delivery constraints and purchases outside delegated limits.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing equipment and materials that fit the work and staff needs.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate order entry where it exists; purchasing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain approved suppliers and purchase controls
reach.learn: Catalogue versions, delegated limits and substitution rules

evidence.claim: Reusing selected catalogue or quote lines in an authorised purchasing flow is model knowledge; the cleaning digest does not establish this particular order-entry capability or saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes need assessment, selection and order placement, not receipt, invoice handling or installation. The scenario requires an existing repeated order-entry fraction; already integrated purchases earn no new saving.

Supervisor produces supplier ID, item ID or checked quote reference, description, quantity, unit, price, delivery location and required date in s2's full40 hours. Missing fields are entered and checked there; free-form or disputed lines stay manual in s3.

Native order reuse comes first. The10 remaining hours in s3 cover final field, total and authority checks; changed lines invalidate approval. Purchases outside the supervisor's authority retain the existing procurement route without assumed free approval.
Incremental4 focal hours cover catalogue mismatch and exception upkeep;2 procurement-role hours cover catalogue mapping. No automatic par level or stock flag is assumed.
unknowns: Current duplication and native purchase configuration
Supervisor purchasing authority and supplier catalogue quality
research_questions: How much order-entry time remains after selection, excluding existing automatic reuse?

tasks.short: Prepare housekeeping activity and expense reports

steps.what: Gather and reconcile activity, personnel, occupancy, hours, usage and expense records
Prepare report tables and charts from the reconciled records
Check report totals, explain exceptions and release the activity report

tasks.design: Configure existing {OPS_SYSTEM} reports first, with controlled exports to {BI} where sources differ. Deterministic tables reuse reconciled activity, time and expense rows; the supervisor retains source correction, exception explanation and final release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate time, work and expense records can require repeated table assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Cleaning operations systems already provide time registration, digital work records and dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Missing hours, inconsistent reporting periods and occupancy definitions that do not match staffing records.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining what the figures mean and challenging incomplete source data.

ambition.what: Review site-level workload and expense exceptions weekly using the same reconciled definitions

tasks.altitude: Less repetitive report assembly; interpretation and accountability remain with the supervisor.

reach.task: Compare site usage and cleaning demand
reach.learn: Denominators and source completeness before comparing sites

evidence.claim: FacilityApps provides time registration, digital work orders and client dashboards; its quality app supports inspection forms, evidence and client reports.
The50-hour table-assembly fraction and5-hour upkeep are provisional scenarios, not measured vendor or local results.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing this departmental report, not performing cleaning, payroll processing, booking facilities or entering supplier invoices. Existing system runtime is not human work saved.

Cleaners produce site ID, work date, completed task and clocked hours in their existing work/time process; reception or facilities staff produce occupancy and usage date/site/count; finance staff produce posting date, site/cost centre, expense category, amount and currency in existing records. Their capture time is unchanged outside this denominator. Supervisor s1 retains30 hours for obtaining exports, capturing missing items, reconciling period/site mappings and marking unresolved fields; s2 runs only on that produced dataset and never assumes complete flags.
Missing source values stay visibly missing and are resolved manually in s1; no invented counts or guessed hours. Test native reporting first; BI is only the fallback for cross-system totals.

Final review20 hours remains in s3. Incremental5 focal hours cover mapping and sample reconciliation;3 analyst hours cover connector access and failures. Added weekly review effort2 focal hours is included within the5 upkeep allowance, not free new work.
Employee consultation and access depend on national rules and the reporting use; avoid individual performance scoring.
unknowns: Actual reporting sources and repeated table-assembly time
Source field completeness and employee consultation requirements
